description: Return metadata about the lot you are currently on: lot_id, human name, shard, community category, size and floors, neighborhood id, owner persist_id, roommate set, build-roommate set, whether you are on the roommate list (owner_is_me), and the other-avatars count. Prerequisite: you are joined to a lot; the VMTSOLotState has been hydrated (arrives shortly after lot-join command stream is live). Effect: none — local-VM read from VM.TSOState, no outbound PDU. Cost: one VM-lock acquisition, trivially cheap. Use to answer 'where am I' and 'who else lives here' questions without waiting for the perception stream's next lot block. Category_id is the raw TSO byte (0=none, 1=residential, 2=money, 3=services, 4=welcome, 5=games, 6=entertainment, 7=romance, 8=shopping, 9=skills, 10=community, 11=offbeat); the string category field is a convenience name derived from it.
call_signatures: cf $CF query-lot                                                                     # no args; returns lot metadata (owner, roommates, category, size)
common_mistakes: These are LOCAL VM reads — they reflect whatever your client-side replica VM shows, which may lag the authoritative state by 1-2 ticks.
lot_id is the DB lot identifier, not the lot location code (24-bit packed coordinate) — do not confuse with visit-lot's target_lot_location.
perception_hints: These ops return the same shape as the corresponding perception slice; use for fresh mid-turn snapshots
Perception already pushes this data at FSO_PERCEPTION_HZ — only call when you need data newer than the last tick
